comment: Increment-3 mutation ledger. Each entry names a module, a unique source substring and its replacement, the wave that introduced it, and the verdict of the last sweep. The set is checked in so the next sweep is a re-run rather than a re-invention, and so a shrinking survivor list is visible in a diff (increment-2 review, mutation-methodology adjudication, amendment 2). Wave 1 (152) was designed before this increment's survivor-killing tests existed. Wave 2 (79) was designed afterwards, deliberately over anchors wave 1 never touched -- a set chosen to be killed is not evidence, a set chosen to reach untouched code is. Wave 2 carries one declared CONTROL ARM (W-M11-CONTROL), a semantic no-op that MUST survive: if the sweep reports it killed, the harness is not reporting verdicts that come from the mutation and every other verdict in that run is worthless. Run with mut/sweep.py in the tester's scratchpad; the oracle is the whole suite with -x, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, __pycache__ purged around every mutation, and the original text rewritten in the finally. Do not run two sweeps concurrently: the increment-3 tester observed one spurious 'killed' (W-J01, 3.12) from CPU contention against the suite's performance pins, which UNDER-reports survivors. WAVE 3 (increment-3 review, 59 mutants): designed over anchors NEITHER prior wave touched -- cost/source.py's snapshot validators, detect/base.py's Finding validators and helpers, detect/registry.py's waste mapping, report/json_out.py's timestamp and identifier boundary, and every line the review's own fix commits added. 54 killed, 5 survived: 2 equivalent, 3 real gaps now closed. Two of the three real gaps were in code the review itself had just written, which is the argument for sweeping a fix and not only the thing it fixed. HARNESS: also verify a tree digest between mutants -- a sweep killed mid-mutation leaves a mutated baseline and the next run reports against it. A mutation whose subject was deleted carries retired: true and is skipped by a sweep; it stays in the file because the finding is the point, not the anchor. HARNESS CONTRACT, added by the increment-3 review after breaking its own sweep: do NOT put a test in the suite that compares a ledger anchor to its module's source text. 44 anchors here are shared by two or more entries and 18 more are nested inside another's, so applying any mutation makes its siblings match neither form -- such a test fails for every mutant and the sweep reports 100% killed, control arm included. Observed: one full run reported 289/289 killed for exactly this reason, and the control arm was the only signal. The anchor check belongs in the harness, which reports NOT-APPLIED. WAVE 4 (increment-4 tester, 77 mutants) covers this increment's four new modules and the two it changed.
operators: control-flow swap: continue <-> break, early return removal
control-no-op: a semantically identical rewrite, the sweep's own control arm
exception-swallow: `except X: raise` -> swallow and continue
guard-clause drop: `if X and Y` -> `if X`; `if X` -> `if False`
literal substitution (string constants, rounding modes, quanta)
negation drop or insertion: `not X` -> `X`, `is None` -> `is not None`
normalization drop: sorted(), set(), tuple(), dict()
rung / branch reorder (R27 ladder, R30 priority order)
set-operand-add: widen a frozenset literal by one member
set-operand-drop: narrow a frozenset or tuple literal by one member

mutations.regression_note: increment-3 review: this mutant went from KILLED to SURVIVING as a side effect of the review's own BUG-1 fix, and was caught only by re-running the whole checked-in ledger against the fixed tree. Moving quantize_cost inside the guard made InvalidOperation and Inexact indistinguishable for every input the suite drove, so R29's central clause became unfalsifiable. Killed again by test_r29_inexact_is_trapped_and_not_only_invalid_operation. This is the argument for amendment 4 (run the checked-in sweep in CI): a fix can silently disarm a check, and nothing but a re-run says so.

5.note: Increment-4 REVIEW. Designed over anchors NEITHER wave 4 nor waves 1-3 touched: `attribute_allowlist` (the R34 oracle itself, which wave 4 reached only through `data-seq`), `render_html`'s section wiring and span-id cap, `_header_section`'s R4 surfacing, `_timeline_section`'s no-timing tail, `_spans_section`'s cost mapping, `_warnings_section`, the four `ESCAPE_TABLE` rows wave 4 left, `build_timeline`'s lane and index maps, `render_svg`'s lane rects, and `cli/main.py`'s two-output staging -- plus two mutants on the review's OWN SpanError.code fix, because a fix is unswept code (the increment-3 review's discipline). First run: 31 killed, 10 survived. FIVE of those ten were real gaps and are now closed: W5-A08 (the allowlist could be widened to admit anything and nothing noticed -- the LEAKING_PATHS shape, in the R34 oracle), W5-C06 (A-d11's "both documents staged in one call" was unasserted, so R11's fail-closed guarantee on the PARTIAL-write path was a hope), W5-C05 (R40's path order in the success line), W5-H27 (R4's "non-zero unknown_record_type surfaced in the header" -- no trace anywhere carried that warning beside another code with a different count, a collection of one in the CORPUS), and W5-H31 (the no-timing note's "...and N more" tail was unconditional-safe by accident). Final: 36 killed, 5 survived -- the declared control arm plus four equivalents, all four of which are the same fact as wave 4's: `report/` re-normalizes what `model/`'s validators already guarantee. HARNESS NOTE, observed: one kill in the first run was attributed to `test_r23_blocked_agent_does_not_grow_quadratically`, a WALL-CLOCK scaling assertion, under sweep load. Re-running that mutant alone gave the real killer. A wall-clock assertion is the first test alphabetically in this suite that can fail from noise, so ANY mutant can be reported killed by it; a sweep must re-check a kill whose node id is a timing test. This is a fourth entry in the harness-hazard list, beside the mutated-baseline, the stale-bytecode and the wrong-tree hazards.

6.note: Increment-5 tester, over the six modules this increment created: narrate/narrator.py (21), narrate/client.py (16), narrate/summary.py (14), replay/target.py (12), report/narrative.py (11), narrate/fixture.py (9). Designed from the requirement text before the sweep was run and over anchors no prior wave touched -- no module in this wave has ever been swept. THIRTEEN of the twenty were real gaps and are now closed by tests named in docs/test-reports/feature-so-i5.md section 5; the re-run kills all thirteen. Final: 78 killed, 5 survived -- the two control arms plus three equivalents, each with its evidence in why_it_survives. The largest cluster of real gaps was `deterministic_paragraph`: five mutations of R43's fallback template survived because every test asserted a paragraph EXISTED and none asserted what it said. The second cluster was MAX_PARAGRAPH_CHARS / MAX_FINDINGS_PER_GROUP / MAX_TOTAL_ROWS, where every expectation was computed FROM the constant -- increment 4's I-H02, recurring; the fix is the same, pin the literal the requirement names.
